segments.speaker: vaisampayana
segments.text: And in course of his ramble, he beheld a black-eyed maiden of celestial beauty, the daughter of a fisherman. The king addressing her, said,

segments.speaker: santanu
segments.text: Who art thou, and whose daughter? What dost thou do here, O timid one?

segments.speaker: satyavati
segments.text: Blest be thou! I am the daughter of the chief of the fishermen. At his command, I am engaged for religious merit, in rowing passengers across this river in my boat.

segments.speaker: vaisampayana
segments.text: O king, the son of Ganga, devoted to truth, having ascertained the scruples of the chief of the fishermen, then said, moved thereto by the desire of benefiting his father,

segments.speaker: bhishma
segments.text: Chief of fishermen, thou best of men, listen to what I say in the presence of these assembled kings. Ye kings, I have already relinquished my right to the throne, I shall now settle the matter of my children.

segments.speaker: bhishma
segments.text: O fisherman, from this day I adopt the vow of Brahmacharya. If I die sonless, I shall yet attain to regions of perennial bliss in heaven!

segments.speaker: vaisampayana
segments.text: Upon these words of the son of Ganga, the hair on the fisherman's body stood on end from glee, and he replied,

segments.speaker: vaisampayana
segments.text: Immediately after, the Apsaras and the gods with diverse tribes of Rishis began to rain down flowers from the firmament upon the head of Devavrata and exclaimed,

segments.speaker: devas_chorus
segments.text: This one is Bhishma, the terrible!

segments.speaker: vaisampayana
segments.text: Bhishma then, to serve his father, addressed the illustrious damsel and said,

segments.speaker: bhishma
segments.text: O mother, ascend this chariot, and let us go unto our house.
